title: GrapheneOS Defends Data-Wiping Function That Blocked US Border Search
excerpt: The foundation behind the ultra-secure Android-based OS is speaking out after an activist was indicted for using a 'duress password' to prevent federal agents from searching his phone.
content_html:
The developer of an ultra-secure version of Android, Graphene OS, is defending its approach after an activist used the operating system’s data-wiping feature to erase his phone and block federal agents from searching the device. 

“GrapheneOS is completely legal. We have no obligation to weaken any of the security protections it provides,” the software developer tweeted on Monday. “Laws attempting to make it illegal or require weakening the security would be unconstitutional.”

At issue is an Atlanta-based environmental activist named Sam Tunick, who had the free GrapheneOS software installed on his Pixel phone. In January 2025, US Customs agents demanded the device's password during a search at the airport. Tunick’s lawyers claim the agents “never read him his Miranda rights,” and ignored his request to speak with a lawyer. When Tunick provided a password for his phone, it was actually a “duress password” that irreversibly wipes a device when entered.

“When the CBP officers entered the password on his cell phone, ‘the screen went black, flashed several times and the phone appeared to restart,’” a court document says. 

The US filed a criminal indictment against Tunick in November, claiming he violated a US law against “knowingly” destroying or impairing the government’s authority to seize property under its lawful control. The Guardian also reports the case might be the first targeting GrapheneOS, which has been around for a decade.

In a post on Saturday, the Canadian nonprofit behind the operating system, the GrapheneOS Foundation, explained that the software offers a range of features to prevent data extraction. For example, one safeguard is the “auto-reboot timer” that’ll reboot a locked device after a set period of time to put the data at rest, leaving all files inside encrypted. 

The group's post subtly suggests that GrapheneOS phones can withstand law enforcement searches without requiring users to resort to a duress password. “People should carefully consider how to use it in an actual duress situation where there can be physical or legal consequences for wiping the device,” the nonprofit wrote. “GrapheneOS doesn't require it to protect data from being extracted from the device, but it takes recovering it completely off the table even with the PIN/password for each profile on the device.”

Recommended by Our Editors

On X, the nonprofit has also said it can do nothing to help US law enforcement recover data from Tunick’s phone. “Data cannot be recovered after the key derivation material is reliably wiped. It's not possible and there's nothing we can do to assist with it,” the group wrote. “Similarly, it's not possible to assist with bypassing encryption because the hardware and software has been designed to prevent it.”

The case arrives amid a years-long debate about privacy versus US investigatory powers, which has been a long flash point with Apple iPhones and end-to-end encryption. In the past, the FBI has called on tech companies to build a lawful backdoor to bypass encryption, but the industry has argued that doing so risks undermining encryption for all and creating a way for hackers and foreign governments to exploit the weakness. 

For now, the case might be a PR win for GrapheneOS, which features official production support for unlocked Google Pixel 6-10 devices. In the meantime, Tunick could face up to five years in prison if found guilty. But in March, his lawyers urged the US district court to suppress all evidence taken from his interrogation, arguing that his constitutional rights had been violated.

About Our Expert

Michael Kan

Principal Reporter

Experience

I've been a journalist for over 15 years. I got my start as a schools and cities reporter in Kansas City and joined PCMag in 2017, where I cover satellite internet services, cybersecurity, PC hardware, and more. I'm currently based in San Francisco, but previously spent over five years in China, covering the country's technology sector.

Since 2020, I've covered the launch and explosive growth of SpaceX's Starlink satellite internet service, writing 600+ stories on availability and feature launches, but also the regulatory battles over the expansion of satellite constellations, fights with rival providers like AST SpaceMobile and Amazon, and the effort to expand into satellite-based mobile service. I've combed through FCC filings for the latest news and driven to remote corners of California to test Starlink's cellular service.

I also cover cyber threats, from ransomware gangs to the emergence of AI-based malware. In 2024 and 2025, the FTC forced Avast to pay consumers $16.5 million for secretly harvesting and selling their personal information to third-party clients, as revealed in my joint investigation with Motherboard.

I also cover the PC graphics card market. Pandemic-era shortages led me to camp out in front of a Best Buy to get an RTX 3000. I'm now following how the AI-driven memory shortage is impacting the entire consumer electronics market. I'm always eager to learn more, so please jump in the comments with feedback and send me tips.

content_html_zh:
在一名活动人士使用该操作系统的数据擦除功能擦除他的手机并阻止联邦特工搜索该设备后，超安全版本 Android Graphene OS 的开发商正在为其方法辩护。

“GrapheneOS 是完全合法的。 我们没有义务削弱它提供的任何安全保护，”该软件开发商周一在推特上写道。 “试图将其定为非法或要求削弱安全的法律将是违宪的。”

问题的焦点是一位名叫 Sam Tunick 的亚特兰大环保活动家，他在自己的 Pixel 手机上安装了免费的 GrapheneOS 软件。 2025 年 1 月，美国海关人员在机场搜查时索要该设备的密码。 图尼克的律师声称，特工们“从未向他宣读过他的米兰达权利”，并无视他与律师交谈的请求。 当图尼克为他的手机提供密码时，这实际上是一个“胁迫密码”，输入后会不可逆地擦除设备。

一份法庭文件称：“当美国海关边境保护局官员在他的手机上输入密码时，‘屏幕变黑，闪烁了几次，手机似乎重新启动了’。”

美国于11月对图尼克提起刑事起诉，声称他违反了美国法律，禁止“故意”破坏或损害政府扣押其合法控制下的财产的权力。 《卫报》还报道称，该案件可能是首个针对 GrapheneOS 的案件，该操作系统已经存在了十年。

该操作系统背后的加拿大非营利组织 GrapheneOS 基金会在周六的一篇文章中解释说，该软件提供了一系列防止数据提取的功能。 例如，一种安全措施是“自动重新启动计时器”，它会在一段时间后重新启动锁定的设备，以使数据处于静止状态，从而使所有文件处于加密状态。

该组织的帖子巧妙地表明，GrapheneOS 手机可以承受执法部门的搜查，而无需用户诉诸胁迫密码。 该非营利组织写道：“人们应该仔细考虑如何在实际的胁迫情况下使用它，因为擦除设备可能会产生物理或法律后果。” “GrapheneOS 不需要它来保护数据不被从设备中提取，但即使使用设备上每个配置文件的 PIN/密码，也需要完全恢复数据。”

我们的编辑推荐

在 X 上，该非营利组织还表示，它无法帮助美国执法部门从图尼克的手机中恢复数据。 “密钥派生材料被可靠擦除后，数据无法恢复。 这是不可能的，我们也无能为力，”该组织写道。 “同样，也不可能帮助绕过加密，因为硬件和软件的设计就是为了防止这种情况发生。”

此案发生之际，关于隐私与美国调查权的争论已持续多年，这一直是苹果 iPhone 和端到端加密的一个长期热点。 过去，联邦调查局曾呼吁科技公司建立合法的后门来绕过加密，但业内人士认为，这样做可能会破坏所有人的加密，并为黑客和外国政府利用这一弱点创造机会。

目前，这个案例可能是 GrapheneOS 的公关胜利，它为解锁的 Google Pixel 6-10 设备提供官方生产支持。 与此同时，如果罪名成立，图尼克可能面临最高五年的监禁。 但今年三月，他的律师敦促美国地方法院压制从审讯中获取的所有证据，称他的宪法权利受到侵犯。

迈克尔·简

经验

我当记者已经超过 15 年了。 我的职业生涯始于堪萨斯城的学校和城市记者，并于 2017 年加入 PCMag，负责报道卫星互联网服务、网络安全、PC 硬件等。 我目前居住在旧金山，但之前在中国工作了五年多，负责该国的技术行业。

自 2020 年以来，我报道了 SpaceX Starlink 卫星互联网服务的推出和爆炸性增长，撰写了 600 多个有关可用性和功能发布的故事，还报道了卫星星座扩张的监管之争、与 AST SpaceMobile 和亚马逊等竞争对手提供商的斗争，以及扩展到基于卫星的移动服务的努力。 我梳理了 FCC 文件以获取最新消息，并开车前往加利福尼亚州的偏远角落测试 Starlink 的蜂窝服务。

我还介绍了网络威胁，从勒索软件团伙到基于人工智能的恶意软件的出现。 正如我与 Motherboard 的联合调查所披露的，在 2024 年和 2025 年，FTC 迫使 Avast 向消费者支付 1650 万美元，因为该公司秘密收集消费者的个人信息并将其出售给第三方客户。

我还报道了 PC 显卡市场。 大流行时期的短缺导致我在百思买 (Best Buy) 前扎营购买了 RTX 3000。 我现在正在关注人工智能驱动的内存短缺如何影响整个消费电子市场。 我总是渴望了解更多信息，因此请在评论中提供反馈并向我发送提示。
